proposal_text: This research proposes to build a recommendation system for academic module selection at Trinity College Dublin. The system will analyse historical student records including module choices, grades achieved, attendance patterns, and degree outcomes to recommend optimal module combinations for current students. The dataset covers 20,000 student records from the past ten years. Students will receive personalised module recommendations through the student portal alongside existing manual advising. The system will use collaborative filtering to identify students with similar academic profiles and recommend modules that led to positive outcomes for comparable students. The researchers acknowledge that historical patterns may reflect systemic inequalities in module access and outcomes. The model will not account for disability accommodations or students who changed programmes. Student consent for the use of historical academic records in the training dataset has not been explicitly obtained.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Privacy Breach
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of unauthorised collection, processing, or disclosure of personal data by an AI system.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Accountability
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk that affected persons cannot obtain explanation, contestation, or remedy for AI-mediated decisions.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Psychological Harm
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of mental distress, manipulation, coercion, or emotional damage caused by an AI system.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Dignity
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of degrading, objectifying, or otherwise undermining human dignity through AI system design or use.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Discrimination
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of unfair differential treatment of individuals or groups based on protected characteristics by an AI system.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Data Governance
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk arising from inadequate data stewardship, provenance, or quality controls in AI pipelines.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Financial Harm
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of economic loss, fraudulent debt, or material deprivation caused by an AI system.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Reputational Harm
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of damage to an individual's or organisation's reputation through AI-generated outputs or decisions.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: False Identification
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of incorrect identity attribution (e.g. facial-recognition false matches) with consequential harm.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Transparency
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk that an AI system's operation, capabilities, limitations, or decision rationale are not adequately disclosed to end-users and stakeholders.

assessment.risk_summary: The proposed recommendation system for academic module selection at Trinity College Dublin poses risks to student privacy, data governance, and potential biases in the algorithm.

identified_risks.explanation: The system will process historical student records including personally identifiable information without explicit consent.
The dataset covers 20,000 student records from the past ten years, which may reflect systemic inequalities in module access and outcomes.
The algorithm may perpetuate biases if not properly designed to account for disability accommodations or students who changed programmes.
Students may experience mental distress or manipulation due to the system's recommendations.

applicable_requirements.requirement_text: Assess whether organisation is obligated to conduct a FRIA (deployer of high-risk AI system).

charter_rights_at_risk.relevance: The system's processing of personally identifiable information may infringe on students' right to private life.
The system's collection and storage of student data may violate the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights' data protection provisions.
